data.narrative:
General Matter is a Series A nuclear energy company founded by Scott Nolan and Lee Robinson that has raised $50M+. The valuation analysis draws on a comp universe of 11 peers—3 public companies (OKLO, NNE, SMR) and 8 private firms including Valar Atomics, Fuse Energy, Nano Nuclear Energy, Oklo, and X-Energy, all operating in the same sector and at similar or adjacent funding stages.

Two triangulation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis, using the $50M total raised as a proxy for current valuation and applying a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical for Series A advancement, implies a valuation of $100M. Peer-median analysis across three same-sector peers at comparable stages—Valar Atomics ($6.0B Series B), Nano Nuclear Energy ($808M Seed), and Fuse Energy ($200M Series A)—yields a median valuation of $808M, with a range spanning $200M to $6.0B. The wide peer range reflects stage and company-specific variation within the nuclear sector.

The two methods produce a triangulated range of $85M to $929M, with a median of $454M. Stage-progression anchors the lower bound, while peer comparables drive the upside. Key uncertainties include General Matter's specific technical differentiation relative to the peer set, capital efficiency relative to comparable-stage nuclear companies, and the degree to which the wide dispersion in peer valuations ($200M–$6.0B) reflects genuine market segmentation or valuation inconsistency within frontier nuclear.
